sentences.text: Following operating deviations, laboratory sampling provides independent confirmation that treatment targets have returned to acceptable control ranges.
The Chief Operator establishes daily sampling priorities based on plant conditions, regulatory monitoring requirements, and recent process adjustments.
The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is also known as Sparrow for local bench labeling during sample receipt.
Field samples are labeled at collection with location, time, collector initials, preservation method, and requested analyses before they leave operating areas.
The Laboratory Technician checks container type, holding time, temperature, preservative status, and seal condition before logging a sample for analysis.

Samples from the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Chlorine Contact Basin, and High Service Pump Header are verified against the current sampling schedule before testing begins.
The Laboratory Technician uses the Alum Batch Ticket to verify chemical lot identity before recording related laboratory observations.
The Laboratory Technician prepares and sends the Sample Chain Slip after verifying that custody entries are complete and legible.
The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench sends the Jar Test Photograph Set after the comparison images have been checked for date, time, and sample identifiers.
Lantern must retain accepted laboratory result timestamps with the associated process trend interval so that reconciliation can be repeated during audits.
Field meter readings used for immediate control are treated as provisional until they are compared with laboratory results collected from the same location and time window.
The Laboratory Technician records any mismatch between bottle labels, bench log entries, and operator notes before assigning an acceptance status to the sample.
If a sample is received outside the approved holding time or temperature range, the result may be used for troubleshooting but is not accepted for compliance reporting.
Calibration checks, method blanks, duplicate measurements, and control standards are reviewed before process measurements are released to operations.
Results associated with failed quality checks are flagged, investigated, and either corrected with documented justification or rejected from the accepted data set.
The Duty Engineer reviews significant differences between field readings and laboratory values when those differences could affect chemical feed, filter loading, or disinfection decisions.

For turbidity and particle-related analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms that sample mixing, settling time, and instrument range are appropriate for the expected raw or filtered water condition.
For disinfectant residual analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms reagent condition, sample contact time, and measurement timing before accepting the result.
When a Chlorine Residual Alarm is active, related grab samples receive priority handling so that alarm response can be checked against an independent measurement.
The Chief Operator is notified when laboratory confirmation does not support the field indication that caused an operating adjustment.
Accepted laboratory results are reconciled to operating trends by matching collection time, sample point, process state, and recent manual observations.
If Storm Intake Mode changes the character of incoming water, the sampling frequency is increased until raw and settled water measurements show stable behavior.
The Backwash Recovery Tank is sampled after return-to-process events when recovered water quality could influence filter performance or finished water stability.
The Laboratory Technician preserves all custody and acceptance records for review by the Chief Operator, Duty Engineer, and regulatory auditors.
